name: Computer Automation (RPA)
description: Robotic Process Automation: desktop mouse, keyboard, and window control for complex legacy software.
capabilities: Visual UI element anchoring and OCR

settings.ATENA_RPA_DASHBOARD_LINK: Remote Control Dashboard (add IP, password and check status)

guide.title: What it is and what it's for (in plain words)
guide.text: This feature lets ATENA "see" and manage the other computers at home or in the office. To do this, you install a small program called the Satellite Client on each PC: it acts as a secure bridge between that computer and ATENA. Everything travelling over the bridge is encrypted, so nobody else on the network can read it.
guide.tip: You don't need to install anything on the computer running ATENA: the Client only goes on the PCs you want to control.

guide.title: Before you start: what you need
steps: The PC to connect must be on the same network (same Wi-Fi or router) as the computer running ATENA.
The PC to connect needs Python 3.10 or newer. On Windows download it from python.org and, during setup, tick "Add Python to PATH" (very important).
Write down the address of this page: you can see it in the browser's address bar (e.g. 192.168.1.100:8080). You'll need it shortly.

guide.title: Download and start the Client on the PC to connect
steps: From the PC you want to connect, open this same page and press "Download Client (.ZIP)". Alternatively download it here and copy it to the PC with a USB stick.
Find ATENA_Satellite_Client.zip in your Downloads folder, right-click → "Extract All…" and pick a folder (e.g. Documents\ATENA_Client).
Windows: open the extracted folder and double-click Start_ATENA_Client.bat. If the blue "Windows protected your PC" warning appears, click "More info" and then "Run anyway".
macOS / Linux: open a Terminal in the extracted folder and type: bash Start_ATENA_Client.sh
The first time, the Client downloads the components it needs by itself: this can take a minute or two. Then a small dark "ATENA SATELLITE" window appears.
guide.tip: If Windows asks whether to allow Python network access, choose "Private networks" and press "Allow": without it ATENA cannot reach the PC.

guide.title: Connect the PC to ATENA
steps: In the Client window, in the "IP Server ATENA" field, type the address you wrote down (e.g. 192.168.1.100:8080).
In "Nome di questo PC" (this PC's name) type an easy name without spaces (e.g. OFFICE-1 or LIVING-PC).
Press "Associa" (Pair). When the text turns green "● Associato ad ATENA", you're connected.
Come back here and press "Open PC Dashboard": the new computer will appear in the list.

guide.title: Everyday use
guide.text: Once connected, you can talk to ATENA in chat using the name you gave the PC. Examples: "How much RAM is OFFICE-1 using?", "Check free disk space on LIVING-PC", "Read the document I'm writing". The Client must stay open: if you close it, ATENA no longer sees that computer until you restart it.

guide.title: Connecting a PC without the Client (advanced users)
guide.text: From the Dashboard you can also add a computer manually with IP, user and password. On Windows enable WinRM (PowerShell as administrator: Enable-PSRemoting -Force); on Linux and macOS an active SSH server is enough. This way ATENA can read the system status, but cannot see open windows.

guide.title: Troubleshooting
steps: The Client window opens and closes immediately: Python is not installed or "Add Python to PATH" was not ticked. Reinstall Python with the box ticked.
It stays on "Riprova" (Retry) after pressing Pair: check you typed the address exactly as in the browser bar, including the number after the colon.
The PC shows as offline in the Dashboard: make sure the Client is open and the firewall allows Python on private networks (port 19999).
The download fails: update ATENA to the latest version; the error message also shows the folder where ATENA looks for the Client files.

help.ATENA_RPA_PSK: No need to change it: it's created automatically. Change it only if you know what you're doing.
help.ATENA_RPA_AUTO_SYNC: When on, ATENA periodically checks by itself that connected PCs are on and reachable.
help.ATENA_RPA_DASHBOARD_LINK: Here you see the list of connected computers, add new ones manually and check whether they are online.
help.ATENA_RPA_DOWNLOAD_LINK: Program to install on every PC you want ATENA to see (Windows, macOS or Linux).
help.ATENA_RPA_NODES: Leave empty. Only needed for old installations.
